title: What a person learns from the Acme Notes release builds

summary.headline: We ran standard tools against three Acme Notes builds. The JavaScript bundle is the exposure. It holds two real secrets, and they are the same in every build.
summary.found: Two secrets are plain strings in the bundle: a hosting-protection bypass token (F1) and a request-signing key (F2). Three map API keys are inlined too (F3).
summary.meaning: Anyone can replay F1 and F2 without the app. Code shrinking and symbol stripping do not touch the bundle, so they do not help.
do_first: Rotate F1 and remove it from the bundle.
Show F1 and F2 to the security team before you write about them outside the team.

builds.name: Staging Android
builds.description: CI release build with code shrinking off.

matrix_note: The live Android build was not analysed. It should match the live iOS build.

layers.name: JavaScript bundle
layers.note: Every build-time environment value is a plain string.

layers.name: DEX and native code
layers.note: Own code is small. Nothing of value hides here.

layers_conclusion: The fix is not a compiler setting. The secrets are in the first three layers. The fix is on the server, or in what the app inlines.

findings.title: Hosting-protection bypass token is inlined
findings.subtitle: Same value in all three builds
findings.what: The app sends the token on every API request. With it, anyone reaches the protected deployment without the app.
findings.evidence: Function sendRequest: LoadConstString "x7Qa…9Z" (32), next to the header-name literal.
findings.fix: Rotate the token. Remove it from the bundle. Use a server-side control, for example app attestation. Keep the old value working until users update, then revoke it.

findings.title: Request signature is forgeable
findings.subtitle: Both signing inputs are in the bundle
findings.what: The app signs requests with SHA1(shared key + API key + values). Both keys are inlined.
findings.evidence: Function signRequest: two long strings, then a SHA1 digest call and the literal "&sig=".
findings.fix: Move signing to the server, or use a per-install secret. Rotate both keys.

findings.title: Three map API keys are inlined
findings.subtitle: The first scan counted two
findings.what: One key is hardcoded in source. One is chosen with Platform.OS at runtime, so both platform keys ship on both platforms. One sits inside a URL string.
findings.evidence: Raw byte scan of each bundle: three distinct keys. The string-table scan found two, because the third key sits inside a URL.
findings.impact: React Native fetch sends no package or bundle headers, so an app restriction cannot protect these keys. Quota theft is possible.
findings.fix: Move the hardcoded key to an environment value and rotate it. Restrict each key by API and quota. Set spend alerts.

findings.title: Build metadata ships as assets
findings.what: assets/app.config holds the full app config: plugin list, bundle IDs, error-tracking project name.

findings.title: iOS token store is unencrypted and in backups
findings.subtitle: Source review. An IPA does not show runtime storage.
findings.what: Session tokens live in the Documents directory with no encryption key. Device and cloud backups include it.
findings.fix: Exclude the directory from backup. Consider an encryption key kept in the Keychain.

findings.title: DEX code is readable
findings.subtitle: Shrinker renames library code
findings.what: With shrinking off, all classes are readable. With it on, about 65% have names of 1 to 3 characters.
findings.fix: None. Keep the shrinker for size and store rules, not for secrecy.

corrections.title: F1 was wrongly reported absent from the release candidate.
corrections.text: The first scan read only half of the string table. The corrected scan reads all entries.

corrections.title: F3 has three keys, not two.
corrections.text: The first scan missed a key inside a URL. The raw byte scan found it.

method.title: Pick the builds
method.text: A staging build from CI, the store release candidate, and the live store build.

method.title: Read the bundle
method.text: Disassemble it. Dump the whole string table. Check the parsed count against the header.

method.title: Re-measure
method.text: Run every count again on the final builds before you publish.

tools.result: Worked. Full disassembly. Found F1 to F3.
Worked. Found the key inside a URL.
Failed. It does not read Hermes bytecode.

hardening.verdict: No. Shrinking and symbol stripping protect code that holds nothing of value.
points: Android shrinker: renames and removes DEX code only. Secrets are in the bundle, assets and resources.
iOS strip settings: remove local symbols only. The bundle and property lists stay readable.

next_steps.title: Rotate the bypass token and remove it from the bundle (F1)
next_steps.text: Check the hosting logs for use of the old token. Keep the old value working until users update.

next_steps.title: Replace the shared-key signature scheme (F2)
next_steps.text: Move signing to the server. Rotate both keys.

next_steps.title: Restrict the map keys (F3)
next_steps.text: Limit each key by API. Set quota caps and spend alerts.

next_steps.title: Run the scan on every release candidate
next_steps.text: Fail the build when a new secret-shaped string appears.

analysed: Release-candidate APK from the store console.
Live iOS IPA: bundle, property lists, entitlements.
not_analysed: The iOS main executable (encrypted by the store).
